_note: HOW THE SIMULATED PLAYER CHOOSES WHAT TO BUILD. This is the MEASURING INSTRUMENT, not the game -- nothing under src/ reads it and nothing here reaches a player. It lives in tools/soak/ rather than src/data/ deliberately: a knob that changes what the soak MEASURES is not a balance number, and a future session finding it under src/data/ would reasonably read it as a game rule and tune against it.
_whyThisExists: tools/soak/Sim.ts chose with `rng.pick(affordable)` -- a uniform pick over every tower it could afford, with no concept of what a tower is FOR. That was survivable while the pool was almost all damage. It stopped being survivable when the Ima Dummy Tower became a guaranteed opener on every level: the simulated player then put a zero-damage blocking tower on roughly one pad in three from wave 1 on every board, seven of ten levels 'got harder' and no level was left in the 35-45% band. reports/2026-09-16-dummy-tower-guaranteed.md proves the cause with a control run -- the tower merely being in the pool is worth +43 runs over 4800 and leaves five levels in band; the GUARANTEE is worth -330. That was a measurement artefact, and `shelter` (the Beacon: +30% and zero damage) has had the same flaw at weight 3 for as long as it has existed, just smaller.
_zeroDamage:
THE CAP ON TOWERS THAT DEAL NO DAMAGE THEMSELVES, which today is the Beacon and the Ima Dummy Tower -- read off `damage` in towers.json rather than from a new field, because a tower whose damage is retuned to zero should fall under this without anybody remembering to flag it. A garrison's lads and a Beacon's aura are real contributions; what the cap is about is that the PAD contributes no tower DPS, and a third of the board spent that way is not a board any person would build.

DERIVED FROM PAD COUNT, NOT FIXED. `max(min, floor(pads * padShare))`, and it followed the boards on its own when the hand-authored plots landed on 2026-09-17: nothing here was edited and every cap moved by itself. The ten boards carried 7, 15, 15, 14, 14, 18, 22, 19, 15 and 12 pads for caps of 1, 3, 3, 2, 2, 3, 4, 3, 3 and 2; they carry 10, 10, 14, 14, 18, 18, 17, 20, 15 and 21 now, for caps of 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 3 and 4. `python3 tools/padcounts.py` prints the counts and tests/soakbuilder.test.ts re-derives every cap from the shipped map. A fixed number would mean the same cap on level 2's ten pads and level 10's twenty-one, which are not the same board.

`min` is what stops a hypothetical tiny board banning the role outright: a blocker at a chokepoint is a legitimate opening and the cap must never read zero.
_firstGun: AND THE BOARD GETS A GUN BEFORE IT GETS ANYTHING ELSE. While no tower on the board deals damage, the pick is restricted to towers that do -- so a run cannot open with a Beacon buffing nothing, which the uniform pick did freely. If no damage tower is affordable for the pad in hand, the restriction lifts rather than stalling the build: something is better than an empty board.
_zeroDamageUpgrades:
AND A BLOCKER IS BOUGHT AND LEFT ALONE. THE THIRD RULE, AND IT HAS NO NUMBER.

The cap above limits the PADS. It does not limit the PEANUTS, and the upgrade loop in `spend` is where the rest of them went: it walked every tower the board owned and tiered it, a zero-damage tower included. Level 6 capped its pads at a fifth and still sent 29.5% of its tower peanuts through towers that can never fire, against 17.1% with the guarantee off. reports/2026-09-17-soak-builder.md is that measurement; it is why the second rule earned a third.

THE RULE: while any tower that shoots is below its top tier, nothing that does not shoot is upgraded. A human buys a wall and leaves it; it does not tier a wall to three while its guns sit at one.

IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT A SPEND SHARE. A `zeroDamageSpendShare` beside `padShare` was the fallback the brief allowed if the simple rule was not enough, and it was not needed: under the rule nine of the ten levels sit BELOW the 17.1% guarantee-off reference, level 6 at 5.1%. The tenth is level 10 at 22.1%, and that is not the rule failing -- it is a long, rich board maxing every gun it owns, at which point the rule lifts because nothing that shoots is below its top tier and a blocker is the only thing left to buy. A person does that too. The rule is about the ORDER, not the total, and a hard share would have banned the correct behaviour to bound the correct number. See reports/2026-09-17-soak-builder-spend.md.

WHAT WATCHES IT: `SoakResult.builder.zeroDamageUpgradesWhileGunBelowTop`, re-derived from the board at the moment the peanuts leave rather than from the rule's own flag, so it is a witness and not a restatement. It must read zero on every run and tests/soakbuilder.test.ts fails if it does not.
_notAStrategyAI: THE RANDOM PICK IS THE POINT AND IT SURVIVES. Past the three rules above, the choice is the same uniform `rng.pick` it always was. A builder that placed towers WELL would flatter whatever tuning it happened to suit and stop being a neutral instrument; these three rules only remove behaviour no player would exhibit -- a board with no gun on it, a third of the pads spent on towers that do not shoot, and a wall tiered to the top while the guns sit at one. NONE OF THEM CHOOSES. No rule here says which tower, which pad or which gun to tier; every one of them is a floor on stupidity. Do not add a fourth without a measurement that says the third was not enough, the way reports/2026-09-17-soak-builder.md was that measurement for the second.
_exemptModes: `supportonly` IS EXEMPT, and has to be. It is the deliberately-broken player -- its whole pool is the Beacon, so a zero-damage cap would turn it into `nobuild` and silently delete a mode whose job is to show where a board cannot kill anything. `nobuild` never reaches this code.
